elements.element: Customer has no obligation to disclose to Vendor any more favourable third-party commercial offer.
elements.evidence: Section 7.2 expressly states that Customer “need not disclose” any more favourable commercial offer it receives.

elements.element: Customer has no obligation to match for Vendor any more favourable third-party commercial offer.
elements.evidence: Section 7.2 expressly states that Customer “need not…match for Vendor” any more favourable commercial offer.

elements.element: Customer is not otherwise subject to any most-favoured-nation or equivalent right-to-match obligation in Vendor's favour.
elements.evidence: The operative sentence “Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation to Vendor” broadly eliminates such obligations, consistently with Section 12.3.

elements.element: Any MFN obligation burdening Customer is limited to a specifically defined product.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: the rendered language imposes no MFN obligation on Customer at all, so no product scope can exceed this fallback limitation.

elements.element: Any MFN obligation burdening Customer lasts no more than 12 months.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: Customer has no MFN obligation, including one lasting longer than 12 months.

elements.element: Any MFN obligation burdening Customer excludes offers or transactions that are not reasonably comparable.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: because no MFN applies, Customer cannot be required to match either comparable or non-comparable offers.

result.reason: The operative redline fully achieves the preferred position by negating the disclosure and matching duties and adding a broad statement that Customer has no MFN obligation. The fallback protections are also satisfied because the MFN condition is demonstrably absent. The redline preserves unrelated fee and business-freedom terms and introduces no contradiction. It is not strictly minimal because the added standalone no-MFN sentence substantially duplicates the revised Section 7.2 and existing Section 12.3; deleting or negating Section 7.2 alone, together with Section 12.3, would have achieved the preferred result more economically.
